finding_both_modules: BOTH RYLR998s shipped set to 915000000 Hz, the US ISM band. India's licence-exempt allocation is 865-867 MHz. This is therefore a factory default of the product rather than a one-off, and any deployment of this hardware outside the US must reconfigure the band before its first transmission. Neither module transmitted while so configured: probe is read-only and config preceded any send.
usb_fault_resolved: The CoreX 'USB port fault' that stalled this experiment since 2026-08-23 was a MISSING CP210x DRIVER, not hardware. Windows does not ship it and Windows Update did not offer it. It presented as a total absence -- GetPortNames() empty -- because a driverless device is not classified under Ports, so the diagnostic filter used to look for it (Class -in Ports,USB) was structurally incapable of seeing the very condition it was written to diagnose. Querying by vendor id (InstanceId like *VID_10C4*) is the check that works.
